handled_verified.error_node_note: ERROR — the wasm ABI's parse-error node, and this analyzer CONSULTS it rather than declining to see it: `rootNode.hasError` drives the error-collection pass (src/ast/real-dart-analyzer.ts:715-730) that reports every ERROR node inside a damaged region as a syntax warning, and ERROR is on the type-mention SKIP list (line 243, rationale at line 3439) because nothing inside a parse-error region is a fact about a well-formed program. Classified handled_verified for that reason, and because java, javascript, kotlin and bash record the identical pair the same way. Added 2026-10-12: `completeness-inventory.loadNamedNodeTypes` forces the ABI pair into every lane's type list, so leaving it unclassified failed section A on a node type the analyzer demonstrably rules on.

corpus_verified.qualified: authentic ProxiCall/lib files: `SessionOfflineBannerMode.reconnecting` -> `uses build->reconnecting` + `contains`; and 2,405 recovered `case Enum.member:` pattern reads (fix 3d4d7fa4)

handled_verified.fixture_only_note: Master review 3 (reviews/dart/master-review-3.md, F4): these 6 are claimed handled_verified and occur ZERO times in 1,294 ProxiCall/lib files, so their verification rests entirely on fixtures that construct them. `new_expression` is instructive: modern Dart makes `new` optional, so `Foo()` is a type_identifier and the node appears only under an explicit `new` — a legitimate reason for absence, but it means the claim is untested against how the corpus actually writes code. DARTD11's question (are these realizable by any Dart source in the pinned grammar?) is still open for all six. Counted toward handled, but marked here so the total is not read as 93 equally evidenced.

_notes.ERROR: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: the analyzer consults it to refuse an emission and report a diagnostic (src/ast/real-dart-analyzer.ts:369-373 (with the module-level type set at :135)), and `extension-type.dart` is a committed fixture whose parse tree contains one — the same ruling as javascript's ERROR row and the php/error-recovery precedent (reported, not turned into a symbol, neighbours survive).
_notes.library_name: RULED 2026-10-18 (DARTGAP5): the node is READ — `RealDartAnalyzer.libraryName` takes the module symbol's name from it (direct child of program, three measured forms: no directive 2,882/3,000 files, `library;` 101, `library X;` 17; the DOTTED names are why the node is read and no regex over text is). No relationship is owed beyond the module symbol it names, whose name the import/export/part edges already carry. Fixtures: library-implicit, library-unnamed, library-source-pins; instruments library-directive-census.ts + empty-library-name.ts.
_notes.constructor_tearoff: RULED 2026-10-18 (DARTGAP6, closed): a constructor tear-off is not a symbol (DARTD3: every Dart constructor symbol is published as `constructor` with the named segment in metadata), and BOTH realizable spellings emit their owed edge through the existing passes — verified by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/const-pattern-constructor-head: in EXPRESSION position (`final f = Holder<int>.new;`) the grammar's `constructor_tearoff` position publishes the type mention as `references -> Holder` with `meta.typePosition: "constructor_tearoff"`, and in a CONST PATTERN the same spelling publishes `instantiates -> Holder` with `isConstructorReference`. The node type was previously classified only THROUGH the open-gap list; with the gap ruled closed the inventory correctly reported it in NO bucket, and the ruling belongs here rather than as a permanent gap.
_notes.record_type: HANDLED (DARTGAP3's type-fidelity half fixed the acceptance; the containment half was RULED 2026-10-18). A `record_type` is accepted by all three type extractors (parameter, return, field) — the fixed five-node allowlist used to drop every Dart 3 record, and 27 return types + 1 parameter regained their declared record type on ProxiCall/lib with 0 relationships changed. `record_type_field` / `record_type_named_field`'s field TYPES publish through the `record_type_field` references position (pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/record-type-alias: `references Named -> Point`); the field NAMES are not declarations, which is why no `contains` is owed. These three types were previously classified only THROUGH the open-gap list; with the gap ruled closed, section A correctly reported them in NO bucket and the ruling belongs here.
_notes.patterns: HANDLED (DARTGAP1/2 closed 2026-10-18; these node types were previously classified only THROUGH the open-gap list, so closing the gaps left them in NO bucket and section A correctly failed). constant_pattern (bare identifier/relational/collection forms) -> uses{isConstantPattern,isPatternTest} via isPatternTestConstant; null_check_pattern/null_assert_pattern wrap the constant and the read descends; variable_pattern/rest_pattern/pattern_variable_declaration -> BINDINGS collected by collectDartLocals (reads publish the family binding spelling); list_pattern/map_pattern/object_pattern/cast_pattern are structural wrappers whose CONSTANT children are tests and whose BINDING children are bindings. Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/constant-pattern-forms + pattern-bindings. Counted on whole units by script/m14/dart-gap-census.ts (ProxiCall/lib 1,294 files + dart-sdk/tests/language 4,554 files).

internal_silent.missing_node_note: MISSING — the wasm ABI's node type for a token the parser INSERTED. This analyzer consults the CONDITION (`n.isMissing`, the same error loop at src/ast/real-dart-analyzer.ts:720) and publishes no symbol, no edge and no payload of its own for the TYPE: a phantom token is not a fact about the source. That split — condition handled, type silent — is exactly what internal_silent records, and it is the same split java, javascript, kotlin and bash record for this pair (java checks both type strings at real-java-analyzer.ts:435 and still files MISSING here). The string `MISSING` appears nowhere in real-dart-analyzer.ts; the condition does.
internal_silent.corpus_silent_rationale: function_expression (767 corpus files) and lambda_expression (17) are silent per DARTD2 — local functions, lambdas and function expressions are not module-level symbols. They were never LISTED, which is what left them unclassified rather than unaudited.
internal_silent.constructor_initializer_note: initializer_list_entry / field_initializer / initializers are the `<this>.field = value` list a CONSTRUCTOR writes. They emit no symbol of their own because DARTD3 rules Dart constructors have no distinct NAME — the FIELD each entry initializes is the symbol, and DARTD13's post-pass already binds its declared type. Master review 3 (F2) removed these from the GAP list, where they had been asking for a symbol the family ruled out, and bucketed them here instead.

_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-dart-analyzer.ts:373); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

internal_silent.record_literal_note: RULED 2026-10-18 (DARTGAP4): a record literal is a VALUE and declares nothing. Its fields are positions (`$1`, `$2`) or names (`count`), neither of which is a declaration, so the literal emits no symbol and no `contains`. The reads of its fields ARE published (`rec.$1` -> uses -> $1 at 0.9 with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown` — correct, because a record literal writes no owner TYPE NAME at the site), and validation/m14/fixtures/dart/record-literal pins the reads plus the absences (no record symbol, no contains, no fabricated owner). Measured: 249 record_literal nodes in 54 files of ProxiCall/lib.

gap._description: Re-scoped by master review 3 (reviews/dart/master-review-3.md, F2) against the LIVE ProxiCall corpus. The previous grouping was by NODE TYPE FAMILY, which made the work unplannable: one row lumped eight record types under 'record type/literal symbols' and another lumped nine pattern types under 'destructuring pattern variables as symbols', and those are very different amounts of work. Rows are now one per DEFERRABLE UNIT, ranked by live occurrence count, and the two rows that were never gaps at all are gone (see removed_from_gaps). Occurrence counts are measured over 1,294 ProxiCall/lib files.

removed_from_gaps.was: listed under 'record type/literal symbols and typed fields'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: NEVER A GAP — they are a constructor's initializer list, and DARTD3 already ruled that Dart constructors have no distinct name, so the row asked for a symbol the family has ruled out. They occur 25+ times each in the live corpus and ARE handled: the field each entry initializes is a real symbol with a real type. Now in internal_silent with the reasoning recorded there. Reviewer error, recorded rather than silently dropped.

removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP4 — 'a record LITERAL is a value, not a declaration, so the question is whether it yields a symbol at all or only its field reads as uses'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: RULED 2026-10-18: a record literal DECLARES NOTHING. Dart records are structural — a field is a position (`$1`, `$2`) or a name (`count`), and neither is a declaration a store key space can hold — so no symbol and no `contains` is owed, and the owed surface is the READS of the fields, which the member-read arm already publishes (`rec.$1` -> uses -> $1, `named.count` -> uses -> count at 0.9, with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown` firing correctly because a record literal writes no owner TYPE NAME at the site). Measured population: 249 `record_literal` nodes in 54 files of ProxiCall/lib (this spec's `measurement` block). Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/record-literal: the reads, the absence of any record symbol, the absence of `contains`, and the absence of a fabricated `owner`. The two node types move to internal_silent with this reasoning.

removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP5 — 'a `library;` directive names the library. Present in most files and low value for a graph'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: RULED 2026-10-18: `library_name` is ALREADY READ — the module node's name comes from it (`RealDartAnalyzer.libraryName`, the ONE function feeding both the published module symbol and every import/export/part edge source). It was never silent; it was merely unlisted in the type census. The counting was already done and is quoted by the analyzer at that site: over a 3,000-file sample, 2,882 files have NO library directive (implicit library = file stem), 101 carry `library;` (a declared EMPTY name, also the stem by convention but recorded as `kind: "unnamed"`), and 17 carry `library X;` (a declared name, frequently DOTTED — `_fe_analyzer_shared.scanner.characters` — which is why the reader takes the node, never a first-token regex). Instruments: validation/m14/fixtures/dart/library-directive-census.ts + empty-library-name.ts; fixtures library-implicit, library-unnamed, library-source-pins. No relationship is owed: the library's name is the module SYMBOL's name, and the edges that name it already point at it. `library_name` moves to handled_verified.

removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP6 — 'whether a tear-off is a symbol or only an `instantiates` edge is an open question, not a missing extractor'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: RULED 2026-10-18: a tear-off is NOT a symbol. DARTD3 rules that a Dart constructor has no distinct name (every constructor symbol is published as `constructor` with the named segment in metadata), and a tear-off names a constructor as a VALUE, not a new declaration. Both realizable spellings already publish their owed edge and are fixture-pinned: in EXPRESSION position (`final f = Holder<int>.new;`) the type mention is `references -> Holder` with `meta.typePosition: "constructor_tearoff"` (pinned by const-pattern-constructor-head, expressionForm row, which also forbids `uses -> Holder<int>.new` and the old refuted claim), and in a CONST PATTERN the same spelling is a construction (`instantiates -> Holder` with `isConstructorReference`, pinned by the same fixture's 6 shapes incl. nested generic arguments and `.new`). So there is no missing extractor and no missing edge class — the open question is answered by the two pinned behaviours.

removed_from_gaps.node_type: record_type, record_type_field, record_type_named_field (the CONTAINMENT half; the type-fidelity half was already fixed)
removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP3 — 'a `typedef` over a record type emits NO `contains` edges for the record's fields … landing this requires an ANALYZER change AND a matching change in the dart tree-truth oracle — editing differential.ts'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: RULED 2026-10-18 with the Lead's confirmation that no paired differential.ts change is owed any more. The gap's premise does not survive measurement of the construct: a record type's fields have NO DECLARATION NAMES — they are positions (`$1`, `$2`) or names inside the TYPE (`start:`), exactly like a record literal's fields (DARTGAP4, ruled the same way) — so a `contains` edge would need a member symbol on its target end that no declaration supplies. What IS owed already fires: the typedef is published (`Pair`/`Named`, kind type), and the record's field TYPES publish `references` through the `record_type_field` position table (`references Named -> Point`). The family precedent cited (typescript-contains rule 5: a type alias over an object literal is a CONTAINER) is about a language whose object types DECLARE named members; `{int count}` is not a type in Dart, and the record-type form's field names denote no declarations. Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/record-type-alias (references rows, forbidden contains, forbidden fabricated owner on the record-field reads — a typedef is not class-like to member-owner-resolution). Measured population: 219 record_type/record_type_field/record_type_named_field occurrences in 38 files of ProxiCall/lib (this spec's measurement block).

removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP1 — 'the family decision: is a pattern-bound name a symbol, a read, or nothing? 353 occurrences in 110 files over ProxiCall/lib'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: CLOSED 2026-10-18 BY IMPLEMENTATION + COUNTED MEASUREMENT. The CONVENTION was already settled by measurement (a pattern-bound name is a BINDING: no symbol, reads publish `uses` with the family spelling `<callable>\u0000<binding>` and `localBinding`); the REAL missing edge was `rest_pattern` (`...rest` parses as `(rest_pattern (constant_pattern (identifier)))` and `collectDartLocals` never collected it, so every later read of the name published NOTHING). The collector now binds it. MEASURED COUNTS (script/m14/dart-gap-census.ts, production analyzer, one process, whole units): ProxiCall/lib 1,294 files — variable_pattern 325/110 files, rest_pattern **0** (measured zero, not assumed absent); dart-sdk/tests/language 4,554 files — variable_pattern 697/99 files, rest_pattern **34/13 files**. The binding-spelling emission is 32,089 rows/1,143 files on ProxiCall/lib and 15,890 rows/2,818 files on the sdk tests. Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/pattern-bindings (positive rest read + record/object-pattern regressions + forbids against bare reads of bound names).

removed_from_gaps.node_type: constant_pattern (bare identifier), null_check_pattern, null_assert_pattern, relational operands, collection-pattern constants (DARTGAP2)
removed_from_gaps.was: DARTGAP2 — 'bare-identifier constant patterns + null-check/relational/collection forms; 103 occurrences in 50 files over ProxiCall/lib; the qualified case is already closed (3d4d7fa4)'
removed_from_gaps.why_removed: CLOSED 2026-10-18 BY IMPLEMENTATION + COUNTED MEASUREMENT. The identifier read pass now has an explicit pattern-test branch (`isPatternTestConstant`): identifiers under a `constant_pattern` (including the null-check/null-assert/list/map/record wrappers) and relational operands (which get NO wrapper node in this grammar) emit `uses{isConstantPattern, isPatternTest}`; binding-destructuring context, `...rest` and the `_` wildcard are excluded because their identifiers are BINDINGS. MEASURED COUNTS (script/m14/dart-gap-census.ts, whole units, shape-classified by grammar context): ProxiCall/lib 1,294 files — qualified 2,661/225 files (the PRE-EXISTING arm: 2,553 reads emitted), literal 1,113, wildcard 160, binding 47, and **test_bare/null_check/null_assert/collection = 0 (measured zero — that unit's patterns do not include the DARTGAP2 forms)**; dart-sdk/tests/language 4,554 files — test_bare **212/51 files**, null_check **31/13**, null_assert **31/12**, collection **273/46**, qualified 360/25, with **107 `uses{isPatternTest}` rows emitted across 31 files**. The occurrence-vs-emission gap is NAMED: it lives in deliberate ERROR-TEST files (`pattern_assignment_error_test.dart`, `invalid_const_pattern_test.dart`, … — patterns inside damaged regions where the read gates suppress by design) and in per-file exact-row dedupe; the classifier's 48 files-with-gap list is dominated by `*_error_test.dart`/`invalid_*`. The per-unit counts above are the non-double-counted figures where they differ, and the difference is the point: the old number could not be split into work items, the new one can.
measurement.pre_existing_gate_failures: ERROR and MISSING are reported by completeness-inventory as in NO bucket, and were ALREADY failing before this re-scope (verified by stashing). They are tree-sitter parse-error pseudo-nodes, and with 0 parse errors across 1,294 corpus files they are not reachable from Dart source. Recorded so they are not mistaken for new.

decisions.question: Dart has no invocation_expression node: calls are selector+argument_part pairs, and constructor invocations are capitalized bare identifiers.
decisions.resolution: A selector with an argument_part is a call; the callee is the leaf identifier of the preceding assignable selector (obj.method -> method). A capitalized identifier directly before argument_part is a constructor invocation (instantiates). Confidence 0.9 calls / 0.95 instantiates.

decisions.question: Local functions, lambdas, and function expressions are not module-level symbols.
decisions.resolution: NO locals/lambdas as symbols (M12.11 family contract). A local_function_declaration still becomes the call-source context for calls inside it; lambda_expression and function_expression are silent internals. SUPERSEDED (2026-09, DARTD8): a local_function_declaration is now a silent fold — calls inside it attribute to the enclosing real function (csharp/python/go parity), and it never becomes a call-source context either.

decisions.question: Dart constructors have no distinct name.
decisions.resolution: Emitted as symbol name 'constructor' with metadata isNamed/namedSegment for Counter.initial() style named constructors; factory constructors carry isFactory.

decisions.question: Dart heritage: extends (single superclass), implements (interfaces), with (mixins).
decisions.resolution: superclass -> extends; interfaces -> implements. 2026-10-18 CANONICAL VOCABULARY (DARTD23): a with-clause mixin is NOW `mixes_in` (it was `uses{isMixin:true}`) and a mixin's `on`-constraint is `references{isMixinOn}` (it was `extends{isMixinOn}`) — an `on` clause inherits nothing. mixin_application/mixin_application_class resolve the applied mixin as `mixes_in` too (one row per applied mixin, same source/target/line). Pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/dart/mixes-in (single, multiple, application class; forbids: extends base / implements / on constraint as mixes_in).

decisions.question: tree-sitter-dart parses builtin types (int, String, double) and generics (List<String>) as type_identifier (+ type_arguments), not dedicated builtin_type/generic_type nodes.
decisions.resolution: All type positions resolve via type_identifier/void_type; generic arguments live in type_arguments and are preserved in the type string.

decisions.question: Where is a field's declared type in the parse tree, and how is it extracted without an O(class)^2 ancestor scan?
decisions.resolution: The explicit type is always a DIRECT child of the declaration container in front of the list (probed dart-typedecl-shapes.ts: instance/static/final/multi-name/top-level all place type_identifier on declaration; inferred `static const x = Ctor(...)` carries none). extractFieldType scans node + declList direct children only. The old parent fallback iterated every class_body member per field — 13.6 s on phosphor_icons_regular.dart (1,512 fields x 3k-member scan); fixed to 252 ms (50x). Same trap hasModifier documents; a bound is not needed since direct-child scans are O(1).

decisions.question: Calls/instantiates emit ONE row per call site — N sites of the same callee push N identical (type,source,target,confidence) rows. Is multiplicity payload or noise?
decisions.resolution: Noise: 192,761 redundant rows across proxicall (35% of 545,208); oracle/fixtures are presence-based so multiplicity was invisible to every gate. Dedup exact rows at emission (first metadata wins): total corpus relationships 545,208 -> 351,722, dup rows 0. Unique-set semantics mirror the rust #383/go GOD9 qualified_calls lesson.

decisions.question: Local functions leaked as top-level Function symbols with empty scope, and became their own call-source context (contradicting DARTD2's no-locals rule).
decisions.resolution: Local-function signatures are not symbols AND not call contexts: the guard skips function_signature under lambda_expression in the symbol pass, and resolveCurrent returns the enclosing function for calls inside a local body (fold). Corpus: the countingFetch/start 'duplicate function' census rows disappear; calls attribute to the real enclosing function (csharp/python/go parity).

decisions.question: Instantiates/calls with no function context fell back to the MODULE (file basename) as source — every const field of an icon class attributed to the file, a name that is not a symbol.
decisions.resolution: extractCallRelationships tracks the enclosing class/mixin/enum/extension and uses it before the module fallback: field initializers attribute to the owning class (IconSet -> IconData); the module remains only for true top-level initializers. Csharp parity: parentContext?.rawName || 'global'.

decisions.question: Top-level getters/setters fell through every dispatch branch (owner undefined, t not function_signature) — silently dropped as symbols while their bodies' calls attributed to a non-declared source.
decisions.resolution: Bare top-level getter/setter signatures route to processTopLevelFunction as Property symbols with meta.isTopLevelAccessor/isGetter/isSetter (corpus: translate.dart's `List<String> get _deepLKeys` now declared; non-declared call-source tail 0).

decisions.question: Are these four grammar rules realizable as parse-tree nodes by any Dart source in the pinned tree-sitter-dart grammar?
decisions.resolution: No. Probe-verified 2026-09-02 across 25+ syntax shapes (prefixed calls/types, scoped library imports, constructor initializers super.named()/this(), typed literals, is/as casts, enum constant constructor args, super formal parameters): none produce these nodes. They are grammar-internal supertypes whose productions are folded into concrete siblings (type_identifier, identifier, selector, object_creation forms). The analyzer's branches on constructor_invocation/new_expression/const_object_expression and typed_identifier formal parameters are retained as defensive coverage and all resolve through the same concrete-node paths. Reclassified from handled_verified per the F6 fixture-coverage gate (M14.0.F6).

decisions.node_type: getter/setter pairs (method_signature > getter_signature + setter_signature, same name)
decisions.question: M37 master-review 2 (2026-09-06): seenMembers dedup keyed owner:name without kind — every accessor pair collapsed to one Property symbol (setters carry the value param)
decisions.answer: owner:name:kind key; fixture expectSymbolCount value/property/Counter equals:2; mutant dart/accessor-pair-collapsed

decisions.node_type: formal_parameter type extraction (tree-sitter-dart has NO type field)
decisions.question: M37 master-review 2: childForFieldName('type') never matched (probed dart-param-children.ts) — 8,094 corpus params degraded to dynamic; this-params carry type on the sibling field
decisions.answer: span-matched leading type child (type_identifier/function_type/nullable_type/void_type) + post-pass this-param->field-type binding (O(symbols), no parent scans); expectParameters pins total:double nv:int sides:int; mutant dart/param-types-degraded

decisions.node_type: mixin_declaration on-clause heritage (mixin M on Base implements I)
decisions.question: M37 master-review 2: on-base is a DIRECT type_identifier child (probed dart-mixin-shape.ts) — heritage extractor only looked for superclass children, so mixin on-bases emitted zero edges
decisions.answer: extractClassHeritage handles mixin_declaration direct type_identifier + interfaces/mixins via existing branches; oracle derives the same truth; mutants dart/mixin-on-heritage-dropped. 2026-10-18: the on-base moved from `extends{isMixinOn}` to `references{isMixinOn, typePosition: mixin_on_clause}` — an `on` constraint inherits nothing, so publishing it as `extends` put two different Dart facts on one label once DARTD23's vocabulary made the distinction expressible. Pinned by dart/mixes-in (boundary 3, both directions).

decisions.node_type: enhanced enum heritage (enum Poly implements Shape / with M)
decisions.question: M37 master-review 2: enum_declaration case never called extractClassHeritage — enhanced-enum implements/with edges vanished; in-file interface methods also produced no overrides
decisions.answer: enum_declaration calls extractClassHeritage; overrides pass covers implements; oracle enum_declaration branch mirrors; mutant dart/enum-heritage-dropped

decisions.node_type: cross-file overrides (@override methods whose bases are declared outside the file)
decisions.question: M37 master-review 2: 34,306 corpus @override sites produced 32 edges — production never passes overrideCompanion (parseFile callers pass no context) and the pass only checked the direct extends base. Fields also faked overrides via un-gated external fallback
decisions.answer: 3-pass resolution (in-file BFS over extends+implements+with -> companion -> annotation-gated external first-parent at conf 0.8); fields can never override; oracle n/a (overrides not compared for dart); mutants dart/external-override-dropped + dart/field-override-fabricated

decisions.question: M37 master-review 2: cascade calls resolved to the cascade_selector's first identifier (a) — the leaf method (c) lives in nested unconditional_assignable_selector children
decisions.answer: callee chain = last identifier across selector children excluding argument_part (args excluded so b..foo(a.bar) stays foo); covered by existing cascade pins

decisions.question: OO family closure #613 (dart-http corpus): a cascade section may hold several invocations (..a(x)..b(y)); which selectors are calls?
decisions.answer: Each selector IMMEDIATELY followed by its own argument_part sibling is an invocation — ..headers.addAll(x) calls addAll (headers is a bare getter), and ..transform(x)..listen(y) calls BOTH (the earlier keep-last-only logic dropped transform). Same per-invocation model mirrored in deriveDartEdges (it previously emitted only the cascade_selector first identifier = getter junk). pinned: family-closure-cascades fixture + dart/cascade-multi-invocation-dropped mutant.

decisions.question: OO family closure #613 (dart-http generated jni_bindings.dart): does a redirecting factory attribute construction to the implementation class?
decisions.answer: Yes — factory X() = _Y; emits instantiates X -> _Y (the analyzer already did; the deriveDartEdges oracle lacked the mirror, making those the only unexplained instantiates in dart-http at 200-file depth). Oracle now pushes the redirect target (private _-prefixed names allowed, so no capitalization filter). pinned: family-closure-cascades fixture + dart/factory-redirect-instantiates-dropped mutant.

decisions.question: First review: `Foo.named()` emitted a dangling calls->named (no such method exists; constructors are literally named 'constructor') while bare `Foo()` correctly instantiated. Same for prefix `p.Foo()` (calls->Foo) and tear-off `Foo.named` (silent).
decisions.resolution:
Receiver-chain walk: capitalized head + in-file named ctor (constructor-symbol knowledge) instantiates the class and drops the leaf call; prefix-qualified capitalized methods instantiate (generated mock code builds this way); static methods (C.create) stay calls. Tear-offs of known named ctors instantiate. Gated by fixture dart/member-value-reads + mutants dart/named-ctor-leaf-call, dart/prefix-ctor-as-call. THE LEAF-CALL HALF OF THIS RULE IS SUPERSEDED by DT-RS (2026-10-10): 'unknown cross-file X.y() stays a leaf call' is no longer the rule — the owner is now SPELLED and carries a declared cause. The fixture's pin moved from `calls m -> y` to `calls m -> X.y`, and the old leaf shape is a forbid row beside it.

[UNION: the version from the other side read — Receiver-chain walk: capitalized head + in-file named ctor (constructor-symbol knowledge) instantiates the class and drops the leaf call; prefix-qualified capitalized methods instantiate (generated mock code builds this way); static methods (C.create) and unknown cross-file X.y() stay leaf calls. Tear-offs of known named ctors instantiate. Gated by fixture dart/member-value-reads + mutants dart/named-ctor-leaf-call, dart/prefix-ctor-as-call.]

decisions.question: First review: `B() : super(1)`, `super.named(2)` and `this.named(0)` emitted nothing on either side — every constructor delegation in the language was invisible (super calls take two shapes: initializer entries and redirection nodes).

Gated by fixture instantiates[constructor->A/B] + mutants dart/drop-super-ctor-instantiates, dart/drop-this-redirect-instantiates.

decisions.question: First review: member reads were invisible on both sides (this./obj./static/conditional access, cascade getters, subscript bases, interpolation) — the managed-OO family contract (csharp CS-R1, objc OC-E) unimplemented, lanes blind by circular consistency.
decisions.resolution: Reads emit uses@0.9 on both sides: argument-less selectors (callee links, plain-= LHS writes and builtins excluded), argument-less cascade selectors (cascade `=` assigns excluded), subscript bases (index-selector shapes incl. assignable-expression targets; declaration names bind via =-position rule), and string interpolation (template-substitution blanket + $x placeholders, labels excluded). Unqualified bare value reads (RHS, args, returns, conditions) need scope inventory and defer to review 2. Gated by fixture (14 uses pins, 1 write forbid) + 4 mutants.

decisions.node_type: selector head whose receiver type the run can NAME but not see (X.y(), a?.bump(), a local declared with an explicit type)
decisions.question: The receiver-availability cut measured 126,295 `calls` and 150,088 `uses` rows whose target stayed a bare member because the receiver's type was not visible in the file, and in most of them the run HELD the type's name. Was the leaf the honest spelling, or was the name?
decisions.resolution: THE NAME. The target becomes `<Type>.<member>` and carries `baseBeyondRunScope: <Type>` — the declared cause whose contract is 'the run that wrote this edge could not look the owner up', which the gate reads ONLY where the target names nothing, so the spelling can never buy a resolution with an exemption. Priced per row against the gate's own key space before adopting: calls +45,861 ambiguous->resolved against -3,892 resolved->unresolved; uses +63,585 against -3,563; 55,973 rows that resolve neither way become a named bucket-3 population; 41,887 stay ambiguous even spelled (two files declaring the same owner AND member). LOWER-CASE HEADS KEEP THE LEAF: a value whose declared type the run did not resolve names no type at the site, so there is nothing to spell. Gated by fixture dart/receiver-spelling (the spelling, its claim, and the boundaries: lowercase head, visible type that rescinds it, visible type that does not declare the member) plus the updated dart/member-value-reads, dart/unknown-endpoint-r7, dart/payload-and-complexity and dart/receiver-cause, with four mutants (revert the spelling; spell lowercase heads; spell without the claim; spread to the receiverMemberOutsideRun branch). THIS ALSO SUPERSEDES R7's suppression of `RemoteFailure.unknown(...)` (`dart/unknown-endpoint-r7`): the row returns with its OWNER named, while R7's rejected alternatives (`load calls RemoteFailure`, the `instantiates` promotion) and the bare `unknown` endpoint stay forbidden — the change names the constructor, never the type alone. Corpus measurement: arm9, against arm8's before-table.

decisions.node_type: a class declared with a PRIMARY/declaring constructor (`abstract class Selector(final Token token)`)
decisions.question: Bucket 3's oracle refuted 3 of 284,377 claims, each an edge whose declared cause named a base the EMITTING FILE itself declares (`scope.dart` claiming `AbstractTypeParameterScope`, declared at line 53 of the same file). Analyzer bug, degraded parse, or oracle false positive?
decisions.resolution: A GRAMMAR HOLE, and neither of the other two: all three files parse FULL (`fallback: null`, `analysisVersion 4.0.0-m12.11-family-contract`) and the declarations are real source, but `wasm/tree-sitter-dart.wasm` returns ERROR nodes for the declaring-constructor form, so no class node exists for any walk to publish. Consequence measured: the class symbol and its members are LOST, and WITH an `extends` clause the grammar's recovery attaches them at LIBRARY scope (a member METHOD is republished as a top-level `function` symbol, `ownerName: ""`), so edges inside such a class are attributed to the library or to nothing. Population, over the gate's admission rule: 440 of 33,738 admitted files (1.30%) and 889 declarations, ALL in dart-sdk - zero in the other six population names - so every dart table in `docs/analyzers/real-dart-analyzer.md` carries this ceiling inside its dart-sdk rows, and no analyzer change can move them. NOT fixed here, and the fix is NOT AVAILABLE UPSTREAM TODAY (checked 2026-10-10): the form is PRIMARY CONSTRUCTORS, accepted for dart 3.13, the grammar chain advertises support through dart 3.11, and upstream tree-sitter-dart's request for the 3.12/3.13 forms (issue #105) was still OPEN on 2026-10-09. Closing it means patching `grammar.js` and rebuilding a shared artifact this lane ships two copies of (`tree-sitter-dart.wasm`, `dart.wasm` - both the local rebuild `tree-sitter-dart-new.wasm`, `reviews/m60-grammar-unmatched-source-read.md`), and any grammar change re-parses all 33,738 files and moves every column of every arm. THE DEFECT IS SHAPE-DEPENDENT, measured over six shapes (`class P(final int seed) {}` and `class P(final int seed);` lose the class entirely; `class P({required int seed}) {}` and `class P(int a, {String? b}) {}` are recovered with the params published as properties - plus junk such as `required`/`int` read as properties; `class P(final int seed) extends B {}` is recovered with its members at LIBRARY scope, a method republished as a top-level function, which is mis-attribution rather than loss; `class P({…}) extends B {}` is recovered correctly). The three oracle refutations are the positional shapes. THE IN-LANE ALTERNATIVE IS PRICED AND DOES NOT PAY (`validation/m14/fixtures/dart/primary-constructor-price.ts`, both sides parsed in the same run after proving an unchanged copy is inert): blanking the parameter list in the analyzer's copy before parsing, length-preserving, gives symbols +233, class-owned +989, edges +2,529, owner-qualified edge sources +784 over 409 files - POSITIVE, and still wrong, because on the NAMED shape the analyzer already publishes the parameters as class-owned properties and blanking DELETES them (migration_runner.dart 40->31, migration_summary_builder.dart 40->26, pubspec.dart 20->14), while a primary constructor's parameters ARE the class's fields: a fix that makes the class parse by removing its fields trades one mis-statement for another, and the honest version would SYNTHESISE them, which a length-preserving blank cannot. 135 declarations in 62 of the 440 files are the NO-BODY form (`class X({ … });`) and are outside the transform's reach (blanking leaves `class X;`); the price instrument's first version mishandled exactly that shape and deleted classes it was meant to repair, now a control. Verdict: the grammar is the fix - upstream #105 or a local patch of `grammar.js`. Watchdog: `validation/m14/fixtures/dart/primary-constructor-hole.ts` asserts the hole is STILL PRESENT (a clean parse, a published class, or a member attributed to its own primary-constructor class each fail the run) and re-measures the population on every run (a project newly using the form prints NEW EXPOSURE and fails), so this entry cannot go stale in either direction.

decisions.question: First review: `a + b` / `a == b` and enum `a(1)` constant constructions emit nothing on either side.
decisions.resolution: Silent by design (both sides): operator dispatch is arithmetic, not a named dependency; enum-constant invocations are declarations (their constants are read via member uses, e.g. uses->a). Documented, not gated.

decisions.question: Second review: parameters, body locals, loop/for-in/catch/lambda bindings, cascade receivers and constructor-initializer params invisible on both sides — every `return depth`, `foo(k)`, `use(x)` silent (OC-E parity gap).
decisions.resolution: Exact scope inventory (frames already threaded; for-in/pattern bindings added to the collector; initializer lists bind sibling-signature params): bound names emit uses@0.9 isLocalRead, mutually exclusive with member reads (gate B) by construction. Oracle mirrors frames, bindings and arms exactly (including the direct-child param fix the first lane caught). Gated by fixture dart/value-reads (19 local pins) + mutant dart/drop-local-read-uses. 2026-10-08 — the target is now SPELLED as a binding: `<callable><BINDING_SEP><binding>` (`BINDING_SEP`, src/ast/types.ts) with `metadata.localBinding`, because the STORE resolves a target by NAME and never reads metadata (`parallel-indexer.ts` Strategy 2 admits a bare name declared exactly once in the project), so a bare local name bound to any single declaration carrying it, in any file. The arbiter verifies the claim by the spelling alone (`verifyBindingClaim`: bindingVerified / bindingRefuted / bindingUnverified) and the separator tripwire asserts no published key contains it. Gated additionally by fixture dart/local-read (+ 2 expectations, 26/26) and the instrument validation/m14/fixtures/dart/local-read-phantom.ts (RED on the bare spelling, then CLOSED, with the counterfactual that removing the separator re-creates the false link), and planted as 4 edge cases in the gate's own control.

decisions.question: Second review: top-level variables/constants/functions/accessors read from anywhere (`return gTotal`, `var f = helper`) invisible — members-only inventory stopped at the file boundary.
decisions.resolution: Top-level values resolve (symbols without ownerName, types excluded); members shadow globals, locals shadow both — all three arms mutually exclusive. Function names as values close the OC-H gap (recursion still calls via callee-skip). Gated by fixture + mutant dart/drop-global-read-uses.

decisions.node_type: labels, writes, declaration sites, type positions
decisions.question: Second review: which bare positions must NEVER read, now that reads are the default for bound names?
decisions.resolution: Named-argument labels (label parent), label definitions and break/continue targets (labeled/break/continue parents), assignment-LHS writes (span-matched, plain `=` only — compound reads per C parity), declaration names (positional), field-initializer targets (first-child positional), callee heads, member-link positions, heritage/type/cast positions (type_identifier), and this/super keywords never read — mirrored exactly both sides. Pinned by forbids (labels, write-only global) + mutants (label/write fabrication).

decisions.question: Second review: `InvitationStatus.declined => ...` under `var x = switch` — binding or test? And member+blanket double edges in `${count}`?
decisions.resolution: Case TESTS never bind: constant patterns bind only through structural descent (record/list/map) to a declaration or for-in head — crossing a switch/if boundary tests (the first lane caught the broad version: 3 MISSING). The member(0.6)+blanket(0.9) double in interpolation is inherited DT1 contract (both sides, lane-neutral, presence-pinned) — ruled, not re-litigated.

decisions.question: When ONE scope declares the same callable name twice, whose BODY does the symbol keep? dart kept the FIRST (the #745 wrong-body family).
decisions.resolution: LAST declaration wins — the family rule (js pinned last, py #748 both). Implemented as one shared `registerCallable` path: member dedup keys by (kind, name) into `seenMembers`, now a name -> symbol-index Map so the later declaration REPLACES the earlier one in place (same identity, later body/params/line) instead of being dropped, and program scope keys on `module:${name}:${accessorKind}` so a getter/setter pair is two symbols while a true duplicate collapses. Measured first, full extent: 2,547 corpus files, 15 genuine duplicate top-level callables (all in test files), 0 member-scope duplicates that were not census artifacts. Pinned by dart/dup-decl-last-wins and the CAUGHT mutant dart/dup-decl-first-wins.

decisions.question: Dart 3 `extension type` was parsed but emitted NOTHING as a container: its members surfaced as TOP-LEVEL symbols (no owner, no `contains`), and its `implements`/representation clauses emitted no heritage edge.
decisions.resolution: An extension type is a container like a class: `extension_type_declaration` is dispatched into the container path (its `identifier[name]` is the symbol, `class_body[body]` the body), members resolve their owner through it, `interfaces` emits `implements`, and the `representation_declaration`'s field (`Wrapper(this.shape$)` shape: `(representation_declaration (identifier))`) becomes an owned `property` while its NAME stays a declaration, never a read. Corpus: 303 declarations over 4 pinned dart-http files. Pinned by dart/extension-type (9 symbols / 12 relationships, including the forbid that caught the fix's own first measurement) and the CAUGHT mutant dart/extension-type-members-unowned. Filed as #935 before the fix.

decisions.question: Is an enum VALUE (`enum Color { red }` — `(enum_body (enum_constant (identifier)))`) a read of its own enum? The DT-F+ declaration-name gate listed `enum_declaration` (the enum's name) but not the value's node, so every constant was published as `uses Color -> red` on the declaration line.
decisions.resolution: No. `enum_constant` joins the declaration-name gate on BOTH sides (the analyzer's `isDartDeclNameParent` and the differential oracle's DECL_PARENTS, single rule stated twice) — a bind, never a read. The constants' ARGUMENTS stay ordinary reads. WHY IT OUTLIVED EVERY GATE: the edge was emitted at confidence 0.6, below the M12 harness's 0.7 claim threshold, so it was filed as `unknown` rather than as a false positive and no gate scored it — the M12 #933 triage is the instrument that surfaced it. Pinned by dart/enum-constant-decls and the CAUGHT mutant dart/enum-constant-decl-read.

decisions.status: FIXED — vocabulary extended and rows relabelled 2026-10-18
decisions.question: Two Dart constructs had no canonical stored value, so each was published on a label that also meant something else, with the distinction living in metadata the store's resolver never reads: a with-clause was `uses{isMixin:true}`, and both part directives were `imports{isPart,isPartOf}` with the ROLE (part vs library) in metadata although the two directions are opposite.
decisions.resolution: The Lead landed four canonical members (`renders`, `decorates`, `mixes_in`, `part_of`, src/ast/types.ts commit df5a03eb2). Dart uses two: `mixes_in` (source = declaring class, target = each applied mixin, same source/target/line as the old uses row, one row per mixin, `metadata.isMixin:true` kept, `evidenceClass: structural`) and `part_of` (source = the file's module symbol, target = the RESOLVED project-relative path, `metadata.partRole` = "part" for `part_of_directive` / "library" for `part_directive`, `evidenceClass: import_based`; unresolvable specifier = NO row, which retires the `uri:*` shape for parts). The mixin `on`-base was a third misfile: DARTD14 published it as `extends{isMixinOn}`, and an `on` clause is a CONSTRAINT, not inheritance — it now publishes `references{isMixinOn, typePosition:"mixin_on_clause"}`. Boundaries pinned so the relabel cannot overrun: extends base, implements list, and `on` constraint are all FORBIDDEN as mixes_in; import/export directives are forbidden as part_of; both superseded labels are forbidden at their old sites. Fixtures: dart/mixes-in (3 positive shapes incl. `= Base with M1, M2`, 9 negative pins) and dart/part-of-roles (both roles, boundary + no-row-for-unresolvable pins); updated: dart/member-value-reads, dart/payload-and-complexity, dart/dedup-and-attribution, dart/flutter-bloc-generic-target, dart/part-of, dart/type-references (note only). Oracle: script/m14/oracles/dart-imports.ts no longer derives part directives as imports (a truth row with no emission would be a fabricated MISSING). HARNESS WIRING STILL OWED BY THE LEAD: differential.ts `deriveDartEdges` still derives `uses` for with-clauses, `extends` for on-bases and (via the imports oracle) nothing for parts, and the dart allowlist has no `mixes_in`/`part_of` term; two mutate-analyzer mutants (the `uses{isMixin}` deletion and the `extends{isMixinOn}` mutation) target the superseded shapes.

decisions.status: RULED — the label is now compared, and closing it took four language facts the first draft got wrong
decisions.question: Dart published `contains` — 7,698 edges in a 25-file sample, the largest single-label blob the M60 label-coverage sweep found — with no oracle at all and no allowlist entry, so none of it was compared while the lane printed a percentage.
decisions.resolution: Written from Dart's own containment rule in script/m14/oracles/dart-contains.ts, sharing no rule table or member list with RealDartAnalyzer, and wired with its allowlist entry in the same commit (full mirror, per M49.G7). Four language facts were found by the corpus, not by reading the grammar: (1) `static final X = e;` is a different field shape from `final T x;` — static_final_declaration_list — and handling only the first derived 2 of the 431 properties the jni bindings' `Arrays` publishes; (2) Dart 3 `extension type X._(...)` is its own declaration node, and the jni bindings declare every type that way; (3) `extension X on int` carries an extension_body, not a class_body, so every extension member was invisible; (4) a Dart 2.17+ ENHANCED enum puts fields, methods and constructors directly in the enum_body beside the constants. The oracle also had to STOP inventing: a draft assumed the analyzer disambiguates repeated members with `$1`, `$2` and fabricated that suffix, manufacturing 233 truth rows the analyzer does not publish — a fabrication on the TRUTH side, the direction that quietly inflates coverage. The `$` suffixes are LITERAL in the source (`static core$_.int binarySearch$1(`). Result: proxicall 100% covered / MISSING 0 / unexplained 2.6% (from unmeasured), dart-http 100% / MISSING 0 / unexplained 0%. 19 gate checks in script/m14/verify-dart-contains.ts pin every shape above, including the no-invention rule.

decisions.status: GATED — whole-corpus exposure watchdog; the 128-class must read 0 and the population is re-measured on every run
decisions.question: Pass 3's first-heritage-parent fallback published `Object.<member>` for members `Object` does not declare (128 rows over dart-sdk, 18 more on the projects that do not publish `sdk/lib/core/object.dart`) and EVERY FIXTURE WAS GREEN while it happened. What fails when ANY `overrides` row names a base that does not expose the member, over the whole corpus, on every run?
decisions.resolution: `validation/m14/fixtures/dart/override-exposure-watchdog.ts` walks the gate's population on every invocation — tracked `.dart` files ≤ 1 MB per project, `parseFile` at production's per-file scope — and for every `overrides` row decides, FROM EVIDENCE THAT RUN HAD, whether the base the target names exposes the member, in three tiers: (1) owner `Object` needs no file evidence at all, because `DART_OBJECT_INTERFACE_MEMBERS` is its entire interface, so `Object.toString` passes and `Object.length` is REFUTED — this is the 128-class and it must read 0 on every project forever; (2) an in-file owner declared `class`/`mixin` with NO heritage clause has its own body plus the five as its member set, so a member absent from the blanked body is REFUTED; (3) everything else — owner out of the file, owner with heritage, enum/extension type/body-less declaration, extension `on` the owner — is COUNTED and never judged, because a `baseBeyondRunScope` claim's honesty is `cause-claim-oracle.ts`'s question and a second instrument deciding it would drift from the first. The truth source is independent by construction (nothing is imported from `real-dart-analyzer.ts`; comments and literals are blanked, declarations are read from what remains) and a body that MENTIONS the member counts as exposing it — over-broad on purpose, since a false NEGATIVE costs coverage the walk prints while a false POSITIVE accuses a correct edge, the one direction this lane does not fail in. A control set runs BEFORE any corpus file is read, on synthetic sources through the SAME classifier, because a control that cannot reach `refuted` would report a spotless corpus whatever the corpus held; any refuted row, failed control or unparseable file exits non-zero. THE FIRST RUN REFUTED 159 ROWS IN dart-sdk AND 157 OF THEM WERE THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN: the body-start scan took a PRIMARY CONSTRUCTOR's named-parameter brace as the body (`abstract class InternalStatement({required super.fileOffset}) extends InternalNode` — the real heritage invisible, the parameter list standing in for the body), which produced 155 of the 159 in a 79-file cut, and the blanker was not nest-aware, so a nested block comment (legal Dart) leaked `}` and truncated a body slice while an interpolation holding a string with the same quote closed it early. Both now scan as the language defines them and both are controls. The remaining 2 were TRUE and led to a fix: every constructor symbol the analyzer emits is named `constructor`, so a subclass member with that name matched the BASE's CONSTRUCTOR BY NAME and published at 0.95 (dart-sdk `pkg/compiler/lib/src/universe/recorded_use.dart`) — constructors are never inherited or overridden, and the overrides oracle's `memberNamesOf` has never carried one as a member. Constructors are excluded from the analyzer's override member surface, the shape is pinned BOTH ways in dart/object-interface-override (case O forbids `CtorSub.constructor -> CtorBase.constructor`; case P keeps `GetterSub.constructor -> GetterBase.constructor`, because the rule is on the constructor SYMBOL and not on the spelling), and the PRE-FIX analyzer FAILS that pin while the fixed one passes. Every run re-reads the whole population and diffs the per-project counts against the committed `override-exposure-baseline.json` (`--write-baseline` records it), so a project that starts producing the shape reports NEW PROJECT, POPULATION GREW or MORE UNCHECKABLE BASES instead of silently widening. Run: `npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/dart/override-exposure-watchdog.ts` (`--control-only` is seconds; a repo list narrows the walk).

INCOMING RESOLUTION IS THE LANE'S REAL GAP and it is large: whole-corpus incoming reads 1,033,665 ambiguous + 170,692 unresolved of 3.4M edges (validation/m14/results/incoming-laptop-b.current.log), with `overrides` the single worst type because its targets are published owner-qualified and the Flutter framework is 0 files in the declared population. Coverage and resolution are different questions and this block answers only the first.
2. THE 20,000-FILE CAP. `BB_SAMPLE_POP` defaults to 20,000 and this run left it there, so the population is 78% of the admitted 25,706 by even stride. A later run that raises BB_SAMPLE_POP should reproduce or correct these ten counts — they are a lower bound on a stride, not a census.
